caseno: Death Reference No. 38 of 1991 with Jail Appeal No. 2197 0f 1991
lawyer:
Serajul Huq with Anisul Huq and Tawfika Karim, Advocates ------ For the Condemned Prisoner. 
SA Hasan, Assistant Attorney-General ------ For the State.
parties:
State ------ Petitioner
vs.
Innocent N Egbunine ------ Condemned-Prisoner
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J: This Reference under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been made by the Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka for confirmation of the sentence of death by hanging by the neck imposed upon the condemned-prisoner Innocent N. Egbunine under section 19(1)(4) of the Narcotics Control Act. 1990 on his conviction dated 19-9-1991 for the offence under section 9 thereof passed in Sessions Case No. 243 of 1990. The condemned-prisoner has also filed the aforesaid Jail Appeal. The reference and the appeal have been heard together and this judgment would govern them both.

2. On the basis of a forwarding dated 31-3-1990 by one SM Nizamuddin, Inspector, Narcotics Control Directorate, West Circle, Dhaka Metro Sub Zone. CR Case No. 91 A3 of 1990 was started in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, wherein it was stated that on 30-3-1990 the accused named Innocent N. Egbunine hereinafter referred to as Innocent was arrested under section 19(1) of the Narcotics Control Act 1990 and after preliminary interrogation the accused was taken their custody and the accused who is a foreigner is required to be interrogated by remanding him to their custody for 7 days in connection with the recovery of heroin in order to unearth the chain of International Traffickers/Smugglers of Heroin. Upon the said forwarding the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate by his   order dated 31-3-1990 allowed the accused on remand   for 3 days. On 4-4-1990 the accused was again   produced before the Court with a prayer for 5 days remand and on consideration of the prayer and the gravity of the offence the Court allowed another 3 days remand. On 8-4-1990 the accused was again produced before the Court with a prayer for 3 days remand but the court allowed 2 days police remand. On 11-4-1990 the accused was produced before the Court who expressed his desire to make statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and accordingly he was forwarded to Mr RK Das. Metropolitan Magistrate for recording statement and the accused made the statement and thereafter he was sent to jail hazat

3. On 11-4-1990 the said Inspector filed a preliminary report to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. Dhaka stating, inter alia, that the Director General of the Narcotics Control Department received a reliable information from Delhi regarding the International Chain of Smugglers of Narcotics. He thereafter instructed the Assistant Director Mr Khabir Uddin to inform the  news to the Director Operation Mr Shahidulla. On that day the said Director was away in Chittagong on official business and Mr Khabir Uddin informed him the news on emergency basis over telephone.   Assistant Director Mr Khabir Uddin gave importance the matter and came to the Narcotics Control room at 41. Segunbagicha and held emergency consultation with the Executive Inspectors of greater Dhaka and reminded them that the name and fame of the country is Involved in the matter and accordingly  directed the Inspectors to handle the matter courageously with utmost sincerity. Thereafter, said Director along with 8 Inspectors went to 1, Gulshan on 16-3-1990 and distributed duties to them which continued until 10-00 AM on 17-3-1990. On return of the Director from Chittagong on 17-3-1990 he hurriedly formed a surveillance team with Mr Sukumar Dewan, Deputy Director and engaged Assistant Director Mr Sadek in charge of collecting news from T & T Mogbazar. Mr Khabir Uddin took his position at Hotel Gulshan in guise of a fake businessman and two probation Inspectors were engaged to transmit the signals using telephone of a local business concern. One hotel boy Md Hanif was engaged for spying. According to the instruction 8 Inspectors scattered themselves over the area of No. 1 Gulshan maintaining liaison between them. Information revealed that two foreigners shall smuggle heroin through Bangladesh, one of them was of dark complexion and another of fair complexion and the information contained the name of Gulshan Hotel. The Inspector gathered that one black man is a boarder at room No. 7 at Hotel Gulshan and informed the Director who in his turn instructed the Deputy Director Mr Dewan, Assistant Director Mr Khabir Uddin and 2 probationer Inspectors and one Executive Inspector Mr Fazle Rabbi to take their position in the said hotel. One Assistant Director Mr Hasan who came from Chittagong was also asked to take position in the said hotel with the duty to ascertain the name of the boarder and it was revealed that his name was Mr Mike or Michael. They kept a very close eyes on the movement of the said foreigners for 14 days. Mr Mike used one Mr Kashem as his guide in Bangladesh and used to roam around Motijheel area, Masks Travel, Grindlays Bank, American Express Bank. DBL Home Bound & Ship Packages, Foreign Post Office. Gulshan Post Office and Mohakhali Garments Office. Inspector Mr SK Nizamuddin used to follow him and in the course of his conversation over overseas telephone which disclosed his talks with Mr Kasem, Mr Bhola. Mr Raju and subsequently, the name of another man who was an Afghan national revealed to be Mr Kashem. Mr Kashem came one day and had conversation with Innocent and a Bangladesh national accompanied Mr Kashem on that day which was probably on 23-3-1990 and had conversation for 20 minutes sitting in Gulshan restaurant. After their   conversation they came to T & T at Gulshan and made a trunk-call to India. Thereafter they hired a baby-taxi and burriedly went to a narrow lane in between hotel Nirob and a Video shop at Nazimuddin Road. The informant together with Mr Abdul Majid followed him. Meanwhile Innocent shifted to hotel  Zakaria on 26-3-1990. There also 2 Inspectors and 2 Superintendents were sent who kept watch over the movement of Mr Innocent. On 27-3-1990 said Mr Kashem along with a Bangladeshi national came to hotel Zakaria and met Mr Innocent. Innocent also   made overseas calls while staying at Hotel Zakaria. On the night following 29-3-1990 Mr Innocent left   hotel Zakaria and boarded at Gulshan Guest House   situated at Road No. 37. One Inspector was sent to stay in that hotel. Informant and other Inspectors  remained scattered near the accused's hotel. Thereafter   on 30-3-1990 at about 10-00 AM Mr Kashem and   one Bangladeshi national came and met Mr Innocent. They had talk for about 30 minutes. Thereafter Mr Innocent came outside 2/3 times and again went inside. Thereafter 3 of them went outside boarding a baby-taxi and 2 Inspectors named Wazed Ali Bhuiyan, PW 2. Mr Abul Hossain PW 5 followed them upto Chawkbazar. On reaching Chawkbazar the  Bangladesh national got out of the Baby-taxi and about 20 minutes thereafter came back with 4   bundles of clothes of different colours which was handed over to Mr Kashem who is in his turn handed" over the same to Mr Innocent. Mr Kashem then got   down from the baby-taxi and Mr Innocent alone came back to Gulshan Guest House and kept the same in Room No. 14 hired by him. A hotel boy named Seraj informed the same to the informant. Thereafter Mr Innocent came out of the Guest House for several times and again went inside. At that time the Additional Director Mr Shahabuddin and Mr Smith went there and had talk with Mr   Innocent in the ground floor lobby at about 3-00 PM. Mr Innocent came out of the room with those 4 bundles of clothes and tried to go somewhere also   riding a rickshaw but suspecting the informant and others he went again inside but he was scared. This matter was informed to the Director. Thereafter the Assistant Director Mr Khabir Uddin along with 3 Inspectors discussed the matter and decided to make a search. Director Operation Mr Shahidulla Khan first entered into the Guest House followed by the informant and other inspectors. Mr Innocent was at that time talking to somebody sitting in the lobby at ground floor. Seeing them entering he stood up and went up stairs in front of room No. 14. Mr Shahidulla Khan asked Mr Innocent about his name, country and profession. Said Assistant Director disclosed their identities and asked about the boarder of room No. 14 to which Mr Innocent replied that he has hired that room for one of his friends. Then the Director called the Manager of the said Guest House to verify the register of the hotel but as the system of the Guest House was different the Manager showed him 2 rent receipts of advance in the name of Mr Innocent. Thereafter one guest house boy was called who informed that the key is lying with Mr Innocent. The key was taken from the accused Innocent and on opening room No. 14 the informant and others entered therein in presence of Mr Innocent. Thereafter the search was conducted and the 4 bundles of clothes were taken out from beneath the bed. After opening the bundles wooden frames came out and in the middle of the frames there were hidden boxes and on opening the same the packets full of heroin came out which were numbered as 1, 2, 3 and 4. Box No.1 contained 500 gram ash coloured heroin. Box No.2 contained 800 gram brown coloured heroin. Box No. 3 contained two packets of white cloured heroin weighing 500 gram each and box No.4 contained, 800 gram of heroin, which was illegally brought inside Bangladesh and on opening the same samples were taken for ascertaining the contents thereof in presence of the witnesses including Mr Innocent. A seizure list was prepared at the place of occurrence to which the witnesses including Mr Innocent signed therein. Thereafter room No. 15 was also searched and a big size bag was found which contained 2 gum pots, two perfumed boxes, wearing apparel of Mr Innocent and an attache containing certain papers including his diary which along with the rent receipt of room Nos. 14 and 15 of Gulshan Guest House were seized. As the Innocent committed an offence punishable under section 19(1) of the Narcotics Control Act, 1990 he was arrested under section 36 thereof. Mr Innocent was allowed to sleep in room No. 15 under guard. At that time he was found very much repentant and confessed his guilt in presence of Mr Sukum, Dewan. Deputy Director. He slept for an hour and thereafter went to the roof for walking. The informant was with him along with the material exhibits.

4. In the morning on 31-3-1990 Mr Innocent was brought to Narcotics Control Room at 41, Segunbagicha. Thereafter on production before the Magistrate a remand for, 7 days was prayed for but allowed for 3 days only and in. the night he was kept at Ramna Police Station. On 1-4-1990 he was   interrogated and in the course of interrogation the name of one Mr Bhola, a retired Major of Indian Army revealed to be the main hero of the International Traffickers/Smugglers of Narcotics who once suffered imprisonment and had link with one Raju alias Troilochan of India and Kashem of Pakistan. It revealed from interrogation that Mr Innocent has a friend named Jeff who was a Taxi Cab driver at Atlanta, in American Atlanta, he himself was also a style Taxi Cab driver and once disclosed about his family's financial crisis to Mr. JEFF who told him about the business of heroin which is a very risky but rewarding job. Mr JEFF told him as to whether he is ready to visit India and meet Mr Bhola to which Mr Innocent agreed. Mr JEFF paid him $6.000 US Dollar together with a letter and asked Mr Innocent to meet Mr Bhola at a hotel at Delhi in India. Accordingly he met Mr Bhola in presence of Mr Raju and Mr Kashem. At that time situation in India was not favourable for traffic king heroin. Mr  Innocent paid $2.800 US Dollar to Mr Bhola and at  the. direction of the latter he came to Bangladesh and received the heroin sent by Mr Bhola through Kashern and also further revealed that Innocent used to despatch heroin by Biman Cargo to Bombay and it was transhipped through Sabona Air Lines to  reach Brussels wherefrom is was sent to Nigeria arid   then to Monrovia. These facts were revealed from the letters written by Innocent to his cousin Charlie. From all these facts it is clear that Innocent was engaged in heroin business and associated with the people of India, Pakistan, Nigeria. America and Liberia. The informant submitted this preliminary report on the expectation that if thorough investigation is conducted it would reveal the story of international smugglers/traffickers of heroin.

5. Informant SM Nazimuddin undertook the investigation of the case and on completion of the investigation submitted charge-sheet in the case on 19-8-1990 against the, condemned-prisoner. Thereafter the case record was sent to the Court of the Sessions Judge, Dhaka who on receipt of the charge-sheet registered Sessions Case No. 243 of 1990 against the condemned-prisoner under section 19(1)(b) of the Narcotics Control Act, 1990.

6. At the trial charge for alleged violation of section 9( 1) punishable under section 19( 1)(b) of the said Act was framed against the condemned-prisoner to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

7. At the trial 17 PW s were produced, of them PWs 4, 5, 6, 11 and 12 were tendered and their cross-examination was declined by the defence.

8. At the trial the informant as the PW 1 stated inter alia, that he learnt about the international traffickers of narcotics on 16-3-1990 while he was in control room along with 7 of his colleagues. On that day Director Operation was at Chittagong and Mr Khabir Uddin Director received information from the Director General regarding international narcotics traffickers from the news received from New Delhi' and showed a copy thereof to the effect that two foreign nationals shall smuggle heroin through Bangladesh, Accordingly, they went to Gulshan area  and kept watch over Gulshan Hotel. Mr Khabir Uddin was staying at the Gulshan hotel in guise of businessman and issued necessary instructions. On 17-3-1990 at 9-00 AM Director Operation Mr Shahidulla Khan came from Chittagong to Gulshan and formed a surveillance team under his instruction and gave charge of a part of it to the informant. Mr Abdul Awal. Inspector was given charge of another team arid the Deputy Director Mr Sukumar Dewan was in overall charge of the teams. Mr Sukumar Dewan was also staying in the hotel in guise of a businessman together with 2 probationer,  inspectors. On 17-3-1990 they saw a black complexioned foreigner. After some time they saw more 2/3 foreigners of the same complexion. As per the information they located a foreigner on suspicion and tried to locate his where about and name by engaging a spy. The spy in no time identified that man as Michael Johnson alias Mike alias Innocent and that he is a Nigerian & American national. The team was vigilant to know the whereabout of a fair complexioned man as mentioned in the information. Mr Innocent used to walk around various places in the city and the informant used to follow him. Mr Innocent also had overseas telephone talks from T & T offices at Gulshan and Gulistan. Mr Sadek, Assistant Director was set up at T & T Office overseas line IT Ex point in those T & T offices overseas line in order to gather the signal transmitted by Mr Innocent to various persons named Mr Bhola. Mr Troylochan Singh alias Raju. Mr Kashem alias Bahal. Mr Aleze, Mr Andy. Mr Charlie in New Delhi. Monrovia and Lagos. Mr Innocent used to receive telephone calls from outside at Hotel Gulshan. Mr. Innocent had a guidenamed Kashem. On 24-3-1990 at about 9-00 AM one fair complexioned Bangladeshi national came to Hotel Gulshan in a baby-taxi and had conversation with Mr Innocent and in course of conversation it has been gathered his name to be Mr Kashem. After sometime they together went out riding a Baby-taxi. Informant and PW 4 Mazid followed the baby-taxi entered into a narrow lane adjacent to Hotel Nirob at Nazimuddin  Road. The informant also got down from the baby-taxi and informed the information to the Director Operation and stayed there keeping watch until 5-00 PM. At that time it was raining cats and dogs. On an instruction over telephone from the Director Operation the informant went to the south side of Hotel Zakeria and stayed in the garage and found a colleague who informed that Mr Innocent has shifted to Hotel Zakaria from Hotel Gulshan. At about 9-00 PM informant saw Mr Innocent talking to Mr Kashem and another Bangladeshi national at the lounge of Hotel Zakaria. On 26-3-1990 Mr Innocent again came back to Hotel Gulshan and stayed there till 28-3-1990. Mr Innocent was seen in the lounge at hotel Zakaria at about 4-00 PM. On 30-3-1990 at about 9-00 AM the aforesaid persons came to Hotel Gulshan in a baby-taxi and went inside and within 15 minutes came out with Mr Innocent and got on a baby-taxi. The informant together with Abul Hossain (PW 5) Wazed Ali Bhuiyan, (PW 2) followed them in another baby-taxi. At about 12-00 noon, Mr innocent alone returned to Gulshan Guest House with 4 bundles of clothes. The matter was informed to the Director Operation, the Additional Director and the Assistant Director who took decision to make a search. The informant along with his colleagues entered into the guest house, disclosed their identities and Director Operation went to the first floor followed by them. It was Friday on 30-3-1990 at about 2-30 PM and they look position outside the room No. 14. At that time condemned prisoner Mr Innocent came in front of room No. 14 unlocked the door. On being asked PW 10 Sharmin a hotel waiter, disclosed that Mr Innocent is the  boarder of room No.14. Hotel manager PW 9 Aminul Haque was also called on and following the  procedure of search they entered into the room No. 14. Condemned prisoner .also entered the room No. 14. The room had a bed and beneath the bed they  found a black leather bag. The bag was brought out  by Mr Innocent and on opening the same they 4 bundles of clothes, on opening the bundles  wooden frames came out and inside the wooden  frames polythene bags containing heroin were found  and the wooden frames were marked as No. 1, 2, 3 and 4 and the heroin therein were marked as Exts, II,  Ill, IV & V. Box No. 1 contained 500 gram of ash   coloured heroin, box No. 2 contained 800 gram of brown coloured heroin, box No.3 contained two in packets of white coloured heroin weighing 500 gram heroin each and Box No.4 contained 800 gram of  heroin, in all totaling 3 Kg 100 gram of heroin. The bag has been marked as material Ext. No. 1 and some heroin was taken out in Text kit. From each   of the packets heroin was taken out as sample and   put them sealed with label in presence of the witnesses for chemical examination and the accused put his signature thereon. Thereafter the informant and his party went to room No. 15 and seized  passport and wearing apparels, and other materials  belonging to Mr Innocent which were accordingly exhibited as material exhibits No. VI-XX as detailed in the seizure list seized in presence of the  witnesses. The informant and his party also seized 2 rent receipts in respect of room Nos. 15 and which were marked as Ext. XIX and XIXA. On  30-3-1990 the condemned prisoner was taken to Narcotics Control room for interrogation and as thereafter he was produced before the Magistrate and  the Magistrate remanded him and on 11-4-1990   Condemned prisoner made confessional statement   and was sent to jail custody. In cross-examination the witnesses deposed that he came to know from reliable source that condemned-prisoner was a boarder in room No. 14 and also stated that the room No. 14 was unlocked on taking key from the possession of  Mr Innocent Witness also stated that he has sent the  ample of heroin for chemical examination to the  chemical examiner through a forwarding dated  7-10-1990 and on completion of investigation he   submitted charge sheet against the accused. This witness also stated that, the condemned-prisoner was arrested on 39-3-1990 and he submitted the inquiry report on 11-4-1990. He denied that the date 30-3-1990 in the rent receipt Ext. XIX was inserted by interpolation of 30-4-1990 in respect of room No. 14. This witness also said that there is no system of registration of a room of the said hotel and the rent receipt was treated to be the register and that the writing on the receipt are that of Mr Innocent. This witness also stated that he along with PW 5 followed them upto Nazimuddin Road and denied the suggestion that the confession was not made voluntarily

9. Mr Wazed Ali Bhuiyan, PW 2 another inspector of the Nercotics Control Directorate belonging to Gulshan Branch, stated that on 16-3-1990 at about 2-00 PM while be along with the informant and other colleagues were in the office at Segunbagicha got the information and went to Gulshan area in order to keep watch over a black complexioned foreigner at Gulshan hotel. On 17-3-1990, they identified the man and by forming a surveillance team they kept a watch over the man. On 24-3-1990 they started keeping watch on the condemned prisoner both inside and outside of the hotel. From 26-3-1990 to 30-3-1990 they took position in the said Gulshan Guest House. At about 9-00 AM on 30-3-1990 Mr Innocent along with 2 other persons went out of the guest house in a baby-taxi and proceeded south wards. He along with the informant and pW 5 followed him in another baby-taxi. The taxi stopped in front of a lane near Chalk Boarding at Chawkbazar and saw that an associate of the accused went inside a narrow lane and after sometime brought 4 bundles of clothes and handed over the Same to accused Me Innocent and thereafter the accompanying associates went inside the narrow lane but the condemned-prisoner alone came back in a baby-taxi to Gulshan Guest House. He informed the same to the higher authority. At about 3-00 PM Director Shahidulla, Additional Director Shahabuddin. Deputy Director Sukumar Dewan, Assistant Director Khabir Uddin Ahmed, PW 2 along with other officers entered the guest house, behind them accused went upstairs and entered into room No. 14. They also went in front of the said room and on asking from hotel employees came to learn that Mr Innocent hired room Nos. 14 and 15. Hotel Manager and waiters were called there. Accused Innocent opened the door in presence of the witnesses. Director Shahidulla ordered for, searching the room and after search brought out a big bag from beneath the bed and found 4 bundles of clothes inside the bag and on opening the bundles 4 wooden frames were found containing 4 polythene packets. One packet contained 800 gram of heroin, another packet containing of two packets of 500 gram of heroin each, another contained 800 gram of heroin and last packet contained 500 gram of heroin which were recovered, marked and seized in presence of the witnesses and the accused. Thereafter they went into room No. 15 and seized, passport and wearing apparels of Mr Innocent. Inspector SM Nizamuddin lodged FIR. This witness identified the accused on dock. In cross-examination he stated that he was interrogated by the informant Inspector on 5-8-1990 and recorded his statement. This witness also stated that he learnt that the accused was the boarder of room Nos. 14 and 15 of Gulshan Guest House. He has also denied that in order to save the real culprit they have falsely implicated the condemned-prisoner in the case. This witness also denied the suggestion that no heroin was recovered from the condemned-prisoner.

10. PW 3 Abdul Awal Khan is an Inspector at present a Superintendent in-charge of Narcotics Control office at Gazipur. He stated that on 16-3-1990 at about 2-00 PM he along with the Assistant Director and 27 other inspectors including the informant went to Gulshan and took positions around Gulshan hotel on the basis of an information. On 17-3-1990 Director Shahidulla formed a surveillance team at the place of occurrence. On 24-3-1990 condemned-prisoner went to hotel Zakaria from hotel Gulshan. There also they used to watch him secretly. The accused came back from Gulshan on 26-3-1990. On 30-3-1990 in the morning accused went out and came back in the afternoon. This witness learnt from the informant that room of the accused would be searched and saw the condemned prisoner in the counter of the Guest House. He along with Director, Deputy Director and Assistant Director went in front of room No. 14. Thereafter condemned-prisoner Mr Innocent unlocked' the room with the key lying with him. All of them entered into the room and informant took out a black bag from beneath the be and found 800 grams of heroin covered with red cloth. 1.000 grams of heroin covered with ash coloured packet, 500 grams of heroin covered with brown packet, and 800 grams of heroin covered with light black packet which were exhibited as Exts. II, III, IV and V and seized in presence of the witnesses and the condemned prisoner also put his signature thereon. Thereafter, room No. 15 was also searched and the wearing apparels and papers were seized. The samples of the heroin was sent to the expert for chemical examination under seal. In cross-examination this witness stated that they kept close watch over Mr Mike as has been ordered by the authority and the rent receipts of the Gulshan guest house were seized in his presence and he put his signature on the seizure list at Gulshan Guest House on 30-3-1990.

11. PW 7 Md Sazedur Rahman, the manager of the hotel Gulshan, stated that on 12-3-1990 Mr Innocent stayed in his hotel, registered his name in the register as Michael Johnson and filled up the registration card in his own handwriting and stayed there till 5-00 AM on 24-3-1990. In cross-examination this witness stated that he knew airport guide Mr Kashem who used to come to the hotel and condemned-prisoner wrote his name as Michael Johnson alias Innocent. This witness stated that they usually filed the form and boarder card with reference to the passport but at a time when the same is filled up by the boarder himself they do not verify the same with reference to passport.

12. PW 8 Binod Behari Pandy, the receptionist of Hotel Gulshan, stated that one foreigner took a room on rent on 12-3-1990 and filled in his guest registration card himself and he booked the room No. 7 who stayed there in the said room until 4-00 PM on 24-3-1990. This witness identified the  condemned prisoner on dock to be the boarder  room No. 7 of his Hotel Gulshan. He stated his name to be Michael Innocent Egbunine. cross-examination he has stated that registration card  contained passport No. A443210 and the passport was issued on 26-10-89 at Nigeria treating him to be a Nigerian national. This witness was examined by the Investigation Officer on 24-5-1990.

13. PW 9 Md Mominul Hoque, the manager of the Gulshan Guest house, deposed that on 30-3-1990 he went to guest house on being informed over telephone and went in front of room  Nos. 14 and 15 in the first floor and found 10-12  persons who disclosed their identities to be the  officials of Narcotics Control Department. He saw the boarder of room Nos. 14 and 15 and 4 waiters of the guest house were present there. The informant stated that they would search room Nos. 14 and 15. Mr Innocent personally was asked to open room Nos. 14 and 15 and when the room was opened  informant took out a black a bag from beneath the bed  and took out 4 bundles of clothes. On unfolding the same wooden frames came out containing wooden in thin boxes and recovered 3 Kgs. of heroin from the   boxes and the 4 packets were exhibited as material  Ext. Nos. II. III. IV and V. This witness also stated that the personal wearing apparels were also seized  together with rent receipt of the guest house in respect of Room Nos. 14 and 15 which, were  material Ext No. IXX and XIXA respectively. He identified the accused in the dock. He further stated that heroin was not weighed in his presence but the informant told him to be at 3 Kgs. He further stated that he went to the guest house on being asked over   telephone from his residence at Malibagh Chowdhury para riding a baby-taxi as on that date  was an off date for him. He further stated that the seized rent receipts are the forms issued by the hotel  authority to the boarder. He denied the suggestion that condemned prisoner has not rented room No. 14. He has denied the suggestion that in order to save the smuggler residing at room No. 14 he along with the staff of the Narcotics Control Department  collusively implicated the condemned-prisoner was a boarder of room No. 15 in the false case.

14. PW 10 Sharmin, a waiter of Gulshan Guest House, stated that on 30-3-1990 at about 3-00 PM the officials of Narcotics Control Directorate entered the guest house, disclosed their identities and enquired about the manager. He called the manager over telephone and on arrival of the manager they went to first floor and took position in front of room Nos. 14 and 15. On being asked as to who is the boarder of room No. 14 he identified the condemned prisoner to be the boarder who has booked the room on the plea that one of his friends shall come and stay there. He stated that room No. 14 was under lock and key and the key was lying with Mr Innocent. Director Shahidullah Khan asked Innocent to open the room No. 14 and the accused opened the room and then search was conducted. He further stated that Mr Innocent himself filled in the receipt in respect of room Nos. 14 and 15 and during the search Me Innocent went inside the room and on search a black bag was brought out from beneath the bed and out of which they took out 4 bundles of clothes, on unfolding the bundles the heroin came out which was seized and small portion of it from each packet was taken out as sample. He was informed by the informant that there was about 3 Kgs. of heroin and a seizure list was prepared. Thereafter they went to room No. 15 and wearing apparels and other papers belonging to condemned prisoner were seized. He further stated that on booking the room No. 14 on 30-3-1990 Mr Innocent along with 3 persons went out of the guest house and came back about 12-00 noon with 4 bundles of clothes and took those packets upstairs through waiter Abdul Latif and kept in room No. 14. He further stated that material exhibit XIX and XIXA are the registers for booking of room Nos. 14 and 15 respectively of the guest house.

15. PW 13 Majibur Rahman Mia is a Metropolitan Magistrate who took the specimen signature of condemned prisoner on 30-5-1990 and identified the same as Ext. 4 and in cross-examination this witness stated that the said Ext. including the name was written by the condemned- prisoner in his presence in English.

16. PW 14 Ranapati Kumar Das, a Metropolitan Magistrate of Dhaka stated that on 11-4-1990 at about 3:30 hours condemned-prisoner was brought to his Court for recording the statement under section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code and he recorded the same and no police was present at that time and he disclosed himself to him to be a Magistrate and also cautioned him that he is not bound to confess but if he confesses the same would be used against him. He also stated that he can voluntarily confess if he so desires and the accused answered in the affirmative. In his cross-examination he stated that the condemned-prisoner stated to him that a Bangladeshi accomplice carried the bundles of clothes to Gulshan Guest house and kept the same in Room No.14. Narcotics Control Department appeared accompanied by hotel staff and searched the room and recovered 3 Kgs. of heroin from inside the bundles of clothes. He also stated that he has not given any certificate in the confessional statement form in rule 8 as to whether the confession is voluntary or true and that after the statement he would be sent back to jail hajat. He denied the suggestion that he copied the statement on seeing the writing supplied by the Narcotics Control Department. He also denied that the accused did not make any confessional statement.

17. PW 15 KM Hamidul Haque, handwriting expert. CID Bangladesh staled that he has examined the writing of one Mr., Innocent and compared the writings with the specimen signatures written by one Mr. Innocent and found similarity in the writing and submitted his report which is Ext. 6. He also stated that the specimen signatures were not sent to him separately and denied the suggestion that Narcotics Control Department has sent certain false and concocted papers for his examination.

18. PW 16 Md Abdul Baki Mia an Assistant Chemical Examiner of the office of the Chief Chemical Examiner, Government of Bangladesh, stated that on 9-5-1990 he received one parcel from PW 1 SM Nizamuddin. Inspector of Narcotics Control Directorate vide Memo dated. 7-5-1990 for chemical examination which was marked as 'Ka' and there were polythene packets inside the packet containing white powder material weighting 4 grams and on chemical examination of the same has found that the white powdered material contained the existence of heroin in the polythene packets. He also stated that the seal of the packets were intact and identified his report which has been exhibited as Ext. 7, 8, 9 and 10. In his cross-examination he has stated that he has not said about the formula of composition of heroin in his report although he knows the formula by which heroin is prepared being mixed in percentage with other chemicals. He has also stated that he has not ascertained the percentage of heroin in existence in the packet in his chemical examination report. He does not remember the percentage of chemicals to be mixed for the composition of heroin. He has also denied the suggestion that the contents of the samples do not contain any narcotics material.

19. PW 17 Md Bellal Hossain who is a receptionist of Hotel Zakaria since 1987 has deposed that on 24-3-1990 he was on duty at the hotel when a black complexioned foreigner came to him and expressed his desire to be a boarder in the' hotel to whom he supplied registration card which has been filled up by him in his presence and he has filled the same registration card which is Ext. 11 and he has identified the accused on the dock. The accused was in the hotel from 24-3-1990 to 27-3-1990 and booked the hotel with the passport No.A666937 stating his nationality as a Nigerian and profession as a student but all on a sudden he left the hotel on 26-3-1999 on the plea of going to Chittagong but on March 28/29th he was seen in the lounge of the hotel accompanied by 2 unknown persons. He stated in cross-examination that in case of foreign guests they verified their passport and the endorsement of the foreign currency therein and then they enter their names in the register and in some cases they keep their passports in deposit. He has also stated that he told to the Investigation Officer that the accused Innocent signed in the register book and was given rent of the room on seeing his passport.

20. After the close of evidence the condemned-prisoner was examined on 3-8-1991 under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure with reference to the deposition of, the PWs, his confessional statement and the documents against him to which he claimed innocent and further stated that he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

21. The defence of the accused as it transpired from the cross-examination of the PW s and the reply under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is that, he has been falsely implicated by the staff of the Gulshan Guest house in collusion with the staff of the Narcotics Control Directorate in order to shield the misdeeds of some accused’s who are involved in the trafficking of the Narcotics and he did not hire room No.14 of the Gulshan Guest house. The papers have been fabricated to falsely implicate him. The informant SM Nizamuddin prepared false papers and he never confessed, as has been alleged by the prosecution, to the Magistrate who simply copied the statement of Nizamuddin. The condemned-prisoner was taken on remand in police custody and tortured with a view to extracting confessional statement and on 11-5-1990 he retracted the alleged confessional statement. It is evident from the order sheet that the same was obtained by torture as he was ordered to be sent to hospital by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate in his order dated 12-4-1990.

22. Upon trial of the case, and on consideration of the materials on record the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka convicted the condemned prisoner as aforesaid. The condemned prisoner has also filed Jail Appeal as stated above from the jail through the Jailor which is heard along with this reference.

23. Mr Serajul Huq, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the condemned-prisoner, has submitted that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove that the accused has hired room No.14 on 30-3-1990 wherefrom the informant and his party alleged to have recovered 4 bundles of clothes in which the heroin was concealed. Mr. Huq further submits that the witnesses are not consistent as regards the hiring of the room No.14 as the PWs 1, 2, 3, 9 and 10 could not conclusively prove as to whether the condemned prisoner was in room No.14 on that date. With reference to Ext. XIX and XIXA the learned counsel submits that in view of the interpolations, change of ink in the writings, those Exts should not be relied on as to hiring of room No.14 by the condemned-prisoner. Mr Huq also submitted that in view of the treatment of the condemned-prisoner on 12-4-1990 soon after the alleged confessional statement on 11-4-1990 as evident from the order sheet of the Magistrate and the retraction of the same by the accused, the alleged confessional statement should have been left out of consideration as the same is not true and voluntary. Mr. Huq further submits that none of the witnesses has proved that the accused carried those 4 bundles of clothes to room No.14 in which the heroin was hidden in the wooden frames inside the bundles and, as such, the conviction for the alleged possession of the heroin can not be sustained in law. Mr Huq further submits that in the absence of any evidence as to the content of the heroin exceeds 25 grams allegedly recovered from the condemned-prisoner, conviction of capital nature can not be sustained in law.

24. Mr. SA Hasan, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the State, submits that the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt through PWs 1, 2, 3, 9 and 10 that the condemned-prisoner was a boarder in room No. 14 and he himself unlocked the room No.14 by the key he was holding wherefrom the heroin was recovered by the Narcotics Control personnel’s in presence of the witnesses and rent receipt of Gulshan Guest House being Ext. XIX and XIXA which was in the handwriting of the condemned prisoner being the receipts in respect. of room Nos.14 and 15 respectively were recovered from the condemned prisoner conclusively prod that the condemned prisoner was a boarder in the room wherefrom heroin was recovered and, as such, the Additional Sessions Judge has rightly convicted him for the offence under the said Act. Mr Hasan has however found it difficult to substantiate the capital sentence imposed upon the condemned prisoner in view of the total absence of proof that the quantity of heroin allegedly recovered from the possession of the condemned-prisoner was exceeding 25 grams.

25. PW 1 who is also the informant and the investigating officer in the case has stated that on 30-3-1990 at about 9.30 hours 2 persons entered the Gulshan Guest House in a baby-taxi. About 15 minutes thereafter the condemned-prisoner came out of the guest-house and looked around suspiciously and thereafter again entered his room; Some time thereafter he along with the visitors came out of the guest house' and got on a baby-taxi. The informant and others followed him. He again returned to the guest house at 12-00 noon with 4 bundles of clothes, and went inside. At about 2-30 PM in the afternoon the informant and his associates took position in front of room No. 14. The condemned-prisoner Mr Innocent was at that time talking to somebody sitting in the lobby at ground floor. Seeing them entering he stood up and went up in front of room No. 14. At the query of the informant party the staff of the guest house told that the condemned-prisoner was the boarder of room No. 14. Thereafter the informant and his party entered the said room unlocked by the accused with the key lying with him together with Mr Innocent and on search brought out a black bag from beneath the bed and on opening the same 4 bundles of clothes were found. On unfolding the said bundles, wooden frames came out containing polythene bags of heroin and accordingly, the 4 bags were numbered as Ext. II, Ill, IV and V and seized the total quantity of 3 Kg 100 gram from the 4 frames and sent the sample of the same to the Chemical Examiner. This witness also stated that they also seized Ext. XIX and XIXA from the condemned prisoner. Ext. XIX is the rent receipt in respect of room No. 14 in the handwriting of the condemned-prisoner himself. In cross-examination he reiterated what he stated in his FIR and that the accused Innocent took out key and opened the room No. 14.

26. PW 2, another inspector of the said department, stated that about 3-30 PM on 30-3-90 officials of the Narcotics Control Department together with the informant entered into the guest house and behind him the accused went upstairs to room No. 14. They also went in front of the said room and on query from the staff they learnt that the condemned prisoner hired the room No. 14. Hotel Manager was called on condemned-prisoner Mr Innocent opened the room No. 14 with his key in presence of the witnesses. The room was searched and from beneath the bed 4 bundles of clothes were found. On unfolding the bundles 4 wooden frames containing packets of heroin totalling 3 Kgs 100 grams was recovered and seized in presence of the witnesses. He denied the suggestion that the accused has been falsely implicated in the case in collusion with the staff of the guest house and also denied the suggestion that no heroin has been recovered from the condemned-prisoner.

27. PW 3 the Superintendent of the said department, deposed that on 30-3-1990 in the morning the condemned-prisoner went out of the guest house together with 2 persons and came back in the afternoon and he along with the accused and the officials of the Narcotics Control Department came in front of room No. 14 and thereafter the condemned-prisoner opened the door of room No. 14 wherein they entered and on search found a black bag beneath the bed and on opening the same found 4 bundles of clothes and on unfolding the same recovered four wooden frames containing packets of heroin which were seized in his presence and he was a witness in the seizure list. He also stated that the rent receipt Exts. XIX and XIXA were seized in his presence.

28. PW 9 Manager of the Gulshan Guest House stated that he was not on duty on 30-3-1990 but came to the guest house on receiving a telephone call and found the staff of Narcotics Control Department along with the informant there. He also has found Mr Innocent who is a boarder of room Nos.14 and 15. Mr Innocent who is a boarder of room No. 14 and on opening the same all entered into the room and on search a black bag was brought out from the beneath the bed wherefrom 4 bundles of clothes were taken out and on unfolding the same 4 wooden frames came out and from where 3 Kgs heroin was recovered which were hidden in polythene packets, the same were marked as II, III, IV and V. He also stated that Ext. XIX and XIXA the rent receipts of the Gulshan Guest House were also recovered from the condemned prisoner which was written by the accused. He also stated that seized rent receipts are the form for registration of hiring of room in the guest house. He denied the suggestion that the guest house officials are engaged in smuggling and in order to save them, they have falsely implicated the condemned-prisoner, a boarder of room No. 15 in the said guest house.

29. PW 10 Shamim, a waiter of the said guest house, stated that room No. 14 Was under lock and key and the key was with the condemned-prisoner, Director Shahidullah Khan asked the accused to open the room No. 14 and he, accordingly, opened it and on entering the room along with the condemned-prisoner and on search informant brought out a black bag containing 4 bundles of clothes and on unfolding the bundles 4 wooden frames came out and the Director informed that packets contained heroin. This witness also stated that Ext. XIX and XIXA, the rent receipts, are of room Nos. 14 and 15 respectively of the guest house and excepting the same no register was maintained by the guest house which were seized by the Narcotics Control officials.

30. From the above discussed evidence on record it transpired that the key of room No.14 was with the condemned-prisoner who hired the same on 30-3-1990 and thereafter he went out together with 2 unknown persons and at about 12:00 noon came back alone with 4 bundles of clothes in a baby-taxi which were taken upstairs and kept in room No. 14. PWs 1, 2, 3, 9 and 10 consistently stated that the key was with the condemned-prisoner who opened the door of the room No. 14. The informant along with the witnesses entered the room and oil search the informant took out a black bag from beneath the bed wherefrom 4 bundles of clothes were taken out and on unfolding the same wooden frames containing packets of heroin were found. It further appears that Ext. XIX which is the rent receipt of room No. 14 was booked by the condemned-prisoner himself and the rent receipt contained his own handwriting which was for 30-3-1990. The Ext. XIXA which is in respect of room No. 15 is also in me same handwriting of condemned-prisoner who is a boarder in room No. 14 and he has not denied Ext. XIXA to be in his handwriting and accordingly the learned Additional Sessions Judge has rightly found that the condemned-prisoner was also a boarder in room No. 14 which he hired on 30-3-1990 and kept the heroin hidden in 4 bundles of clothes brought by him in a baby-taxi at about 12-00 noon on 30-3-1990. Accordingly, we find that the learned Additional Sessions Judge rightly arrived at the finding on consideration of the evidence of PWs 1-3, 9 and 10 together with the documentary evidence that the accused condemned-prisoner hired both rooms of Gulshan Guest House and a boarder there on 30-3-90 and the informant party recovered the heroin from room No. 14 which was under complete control and possession of the condemned-prisoner.

31. We have perused the impugned judgment and the evidence on record and find no reason to disagree with the findings of the learned Additional Sessions Judge as regards the confessional statement of the condemned-prisoner which was made on 11-4-1990 and subsequently retracted by the condemned-prisoner on 11-5-1990. The accused was produced before the Magistrate on 11-4-1990 from the police remand when he expressed his desire to make confessional statement but has not complained about torture either to the Court or the Magistrate before whom he confessed but from the order date 12-4-90 it appears that he was asked to be treated but nothing therein has been mentioned regarding the reasons for such treatment. We find that the learned Additional Sessions Judge considered the evidence of PWs 2, 5, 10 and 12 and found that the accused confessed his guilt in the light of the charge brought against him and was of the view that in the light of all evidence taken together with the confession as a whole the confession was true and voluntary. We also find that the confession was not obtained by torture and the confession though retracted can in law validly form the basis of conviction as the same is true and voluntary in the facts, circumstances and evidence on record.

32. The learned Additional Sessions Judge also found, apart from the confessional statement that the prosecution has successfully connected the accused with the commission of offence in question by cogent evidence

33. We are also of the view that the prosecution has been able to prove the case against the condemned-prisoner beyond reasonable doubt as to the charge of the offence of possession of heroin as provided under section 19(1) of the Narcotics Control Act, 1990 and made himself liable to be punished under section 19(1) thereof and accordingly we affirm the conviction of the condemned-prisoner

34. Now coming to the sentence as has been submitted by the learned Counsel for the condemned-prisoner, let us consider relevant provision of section 19 which reads as under:

19 Penalty for breach of provision of section 9

(1) If any person violates any provision of section 9 relating to the narcotics specified in column 2 of the following table, other than sub-sections 1 and 2 of section 9 relating to cultivation, he shall be punished with the penalty mentioned in column (3) of the Table against the said narcotics, viz:

Sl No. 1.-- Name of drugs----Heroin, Cocaine and Coco derivatives ----- Penalty----(a) If the quaintly of narcotics does not exceed 25 grams imprisonment for a term which shall not be less then 2 years and shall not exceed 10 years. (b) If the quaintly of narcotics exceed 25 grams-death sentence or imprisonment for life

35. We find from the table 1(a) above that if recovered quantity of heroin does not exceed 25 grams the penalty would be for imprisonment for a term which shall not be less then 2 years and shall not exceed 10 years and under (b) if the quantity of heroin exceeds 25 grams the penalty would be death sentence or imprisonment for life.

36. In this respect reference may be made to the deposition of PW 16 Abdul Baqui Mia, an Assistant Chemical Examiner of the office of the Chief Chemical Examiner of Bangladesh who has stated that he has found existence of heroin in the polythene packets containing certain white powder substance and also said that the parcels were found intact and he has further categorically stated in his  reports Ext. 7, 8, 9 and 10 that although there is existence of heroin in the said packets but he has not ascertained-the percentage in the sample examined by him. We have perused the reports of the Chemical Examiner. We do not find any mention of the percentage of the heroin found in the sample so as to enable us to ascertain the overall contents of heroin in the said packets. The Chemical Examiner did not determine the percentage of heroin at the time of Chemical Examination. In other words, there is nothing for us to ascertain the quantity of heroin in order to arrive at a finding that the heroin recovered exceeds 25 grams out of total 3 Kgs 100 grams of seized substance. But the learned Additional Sessions Judge in the absence of any evidence as to the percentage illegally considered the entire seized substance as heroin as it contains elements of heroin and illegally awarded the capital sentence.

<u>37. We are of the view that the onus of proving the quantity of heroin contained in the seized article is on the prosecution and in our opinion, the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the quantity of heroin in the entire seized substance. In the absence of any proof that the quantity of heroin exceeds 25 grams the condemned-prisoner is liable to be sentenced under (a) of item I of Table appended to section 19(1) of the Act.</u>

<u>38. It appears from the record that the accused was sentenced to death on 19-9-1991 and for the last 2 years 9 months he is under the agony of death sentence in the deadly condemned cell as a condemned-prisoner. Considering that aspect of the case and the quantity of the heroin does not exceed 25 grams, we are inclined to hold that ends of justice would best be served if the sentence of death be commuted to 5 years rigorous imprisonment.</u>

39. In the premises aforesaid, the reference is rejected and the conviction of the accused is maintained but he is sentenced to suffer 5 years rigorous imprisonment under serial No.1 (a) of table 1 appended to section 19(1) providing penalty for breach of the provision of section 9 of Narcotics Control Act. 1990. The Jail Appeal is accordingly dismissed with the modification of the sentence as aforesaid. Let the condemned-prisoner Innocent N. Egbunine be transferred from the condemned cell to the cell meant for the convicts of like nature.

End.
